plotHelp.confusion_matrix: Rows are actual classes and columns are predicted classes. The diagonal contains correct predictions; off-diagonal values show which classes are confused.
plotHelp.roc_curve: Compares sensitivity and false positives across thresholds. Curves near the upper-left corner and higher AUC are better; the diagonal is the random baseline.
plotHelp.precision_recall_curve: Shows the precision-recall tradeoff. Curves above prevalence and higher AP are better, especially for imbalanced classes.
plotHelp.probability_distribution: Shows how predicted probabilities are distributed by class. Greater separation may indicate better discrimination but does not guarantee calibration.
plotHelp.actual_vs_predicted: Compares actual and predicted values. Points near the diagonal represent more accurate predictions.
plotHelp.residual_plot: Shows errors against predicted values. Random residuals around zero are desirable; patterns suggest bias or uncaptured nonlinearity.
plotHelp.residual_distribution: Shows error frequency. A narrow distribution centered around zero is preferable.
plotHelp.feature_importance: Ranks features by mean absolute SHAP value. It shows average influence magnitude, not direction or causality.
plotHelp.shap_summary: Each point is a SHAP contribution for one sample and class. Positive values increase the class output and negative values reduce it; they do not imply causality.
plotHelp.learning_curve: Shows validation performance as training data grows. Plateaus suggest limited gains from more rows; instability suggests high variance.
